intro: Turn your data, BI, and automation foundation into applications customers can use, trust, and operate.

resources.title: The Python Tutorial
resources.note: Refresh modules, exceptions, classes, and environments; skip syntax you can already demonstrate.

resources.title: Overview of HTTP
resources.note: Understand requests, responses, headers, status codes, and the browser/server boundary.

resources.title: Get started with pytest
resources.note: Use fixtures, assertions, and failure cases to verify real service behavior.

resources.title: FastAPI tutorial
resources.note: Build a typed service with validation, dependencies, security, and database access.

resources.title: Testing a FastAPI application
resources.note: Test HTTP responses and error paths with TestClient and pytest.

resources.title: PostgreSQL tutorial
resources.note: Extend your SQL into application transactions, constraints, and operational data access.

resources.title: The TypeScript handbook
resources.note: Start with JavaScript fundamentals, then learn types, narrowing, and async API calls.

resources.title: React quick start
resources.note: Learn enough components, forms, state, and accessibility to build one useful customer screen.

resources.title: Enable queue mode
resources.note: Map worker, Redis, database, and webhook responsibilities to your existing stack.

resources.title: Docker Compose documentation
resources.note: Practice a reproducible service stack, health checks, volumes, and configuration.

resources.title: Observability primer
resources.note: Connect logs, metrics, and traces to a real customer request and its outcome.

resources.title: Top 10 for LLM applications
resources.note: Review prompt injection, data disclosure, excessive agency, and resource consumption.

resources.title: Qdrant documentation
resources.note: Use metadata filtering, retrieval evaluation, and access boundaries in a small RAG project.

resources.title: What is MCP?
resources.note: Learn the client/server/tool boundary, then expose a single narrow read-only tool.

resources.title: Building effective agents
resources.note: Study the workflow-versus-agent distinction and simple composable patterns; implementation tooling has evolved since publication.

resources.title: Demystifying evals for AI agents
resources.note: Design tasks, graders, and regression cases before judging a pilot by its best demo.

resources.title: Describe Azure architecture and services
resources.note: Use one cloud to learn identity, networking, compute, and storage. A certification is optional.

resources.title: Creating a GitHub Pages site
resources.note: This roadmap is a static website. APIs, databases, and secret keys belong in a separate runtime.

resources.title: Forward Deployed Engineer role
resources.note: Example of customer-embedded AI delivery. Location and travel requirements vary; this is a role reference, not a remote-job recommendation.

resources.title: Forward Deployed Software Engineer role
resources.note: Example of engineering across customer problems, data, applications, and deployment. Job listings can close.

resources.title: Forward Deployed Engineer roadmap
resources.note: Visual inspiration and a broader community reference. Fieldnotes has an original curriculum and design and is not affiliated with roadmap.sh.

resources.title: Sohila’s Python Learning Roadmap
resources.note: A focused branch with Boot.dev chapters, ITI Arabic, CS50P practice, original exercises and data-tool projects. Use the diagnostic and exit checks, then return to the FDE application path.

phases.title: Frame the problem
phases.outcome: A scoped customer problem, a reproducible data baseline, and a tested integration script.

topics.title: Customer discovery
topics.label: Start here
topics.summary: Find the workflow that hurts before choosing a technology.
topics.bridge: Your KPI and dashboard work is a starting point for asking operational questions. Add direct user discovery and an explicit scope agreement.
learn: Map one user's current workflow, workarounds, and decision points.
Separate the buyer, daily user, technical owner, and approver.
Write a measurable outcome, constraints, assumptions, and exclusions.
topics.artifact: A one-page brief for a fictional Egyptian SME: problem, user, baseline, success metric, and a two-week pilot scope.
topics.gate: You can explain who has the problem, how it is handled today, and how the pilot would be accepted without naming a tool.

topics.title: Data & KPI baseline
topics.label: Build on BI
topics.summary: Turn a business question into an auditable measurement.
topics.bridge: Reuse Power BI, DAX, dimensional modeling, and your PixelFed data contracts. Familiarity is a starting advantage, not an automatic completed topic.
learn: Define metric grain, population, refresh frequency, and ownership.
Record missingness, duplicates, lineage, and source limitations.
Keep observed values separate from synthetic fixtures and projected benefits.
topics.artifact: A data contract and baseline table for creator activity or support workflow handling time.
topics.gate: A peer can reproduce the metric from the documented source; synthetic records and unknowns are clearly labeled.

topics.title: Python as a service skill
topics.label: Build on Python
topics.summary: Move from useful scripts to code another engineer can maintain.
topics.bridge: Keep your Python and ETL experience. Focus on interfaces, packaging, exceptions, configuration, and small testable functions. If you need a deeper Python pass, follow the linked Python Learning Roadmap before returning to service and API work.
learn: Use modules, type hints, logging, and a reproducible environment.
Separate I/O, transformation, and business rules.
Handle errors deliberately and keep secrets out of code.
topics.artifact: A small installable or module-based ingestion utility with configuration and a repeatable example command.
topics.gate: A clean checkout can run the utility with a fixture; bad input produces an actionable error and no partial write.

topics.title: HTTP & API integration
topics.label: Strengthen
topics.summary: Understand what actually happens across an integration boundary.
topics.bridge: Build on your networking labs and n8n HTTP Request workflows. Implement one integration directly in Python.
learn: Explain methods, headers, status codes, pagination, and TLS at a practical level.
Set timeouts; distinguish retryable failures from invalid requests.
Handle authentication, rate limits, and idempotency expectations.
topics.artifact: An API client against a local mock with pagination, timeout handling, and bounded retries.
topics.gate: Demonstrate a timeout, a 429, an invalid credential, and a successful paginated response without leaking credentials.

topics.title: SQL integration contracts
topics.label: Build on SQL
topics.summary: Make database access correct, bounded, and predictable.
topics.bridge: Use your PostgreSQL and SQL Server background. Add the perspective of an application consuming your data.
learn: Define keys, null semantics, and query result contracts.
Use parameterized queries, scoped permissions, and sensible indexes.
Inspect a query plan and bound result sizes.
topics.artifact: A read-only query layer over synthetic PixelFed gold aggregates with freshness metadata.
topics.gate: A parameter cannot change SQL structure; missing data and empty results are handled explicitly.

topics.title: Git, tests & review
topics.label: Engineering habit
topics.summary: Make a change reviewable and prove its behavior.
topics.bridge: You already work with GitHub, PRs, and CI. Add meaningful tests around the integration boundaries you own.
learn: Use focused branches, small commits, and a clear PR description.
Write fixtures and tests for success, invalid input, and dependency failure.
Document one debugging investigation and the evidence that resolved it.
topics.artifact: A reviewed PR with a test suite for the API client and query layer.
topics.gate: Tests fail when a real contract is broken; the README reproduces both the happy path and a failure case.

tasks: Draft the discovery brief and list five questions for a user.
Define a baseline, source limitations, and success criteria.
Refactor one ingestion utility into small modules.
Use a fixture and document configuration and failures.
Build a bounded API client against a local mock.
Add a parameterized read-only SQL query and freshness check.
Test invalid input, missing data, timeout, and rate limiting.
Open a reviewable PR and record a three-minute walkthrough.

phases.title: Ship a useful application
phases.outcome: Project 01: a working operations console with a typed API, a small UI, and access checks.

topics.title: Typed Python APIs
topics.label: Priority gap
topics.summary: Expose a business capability through a clear, validated API.
topics.bridge: Wrap the logic you already understand in a service rather than rebuilding your analytics stack.
learn: Build request/response models, validation, and consistent error responses.
Separate routes, business logic, and data access.
Test the API contract and document sample requests.
topics.artifact: FastAPI endpoints for creator metrics, freshness, and data-quality summaries.
topics.gate: Valid, invalid, missing, and unauthorized requests have tested responses; the API never returns raw sensitive rows.

topics.title: Transactions & migrations
topics.label: Go deeper
topics.summary: Own the lifecycle of application data, not just SELECT queries.
topics.bridge: Your data-modeling skills transfer well. Add constraints, atomic writes, schema migration, and connection management.
learn: Model a small operational table with constraints.
Use transactions and a versioned migration approach.
Practice a failed write and a tested recovery path.
topics.artifact: A synthetic issue-triage table with migration scripts and an atomic update test.
topics.gate: A failed multi-step operation leaves consistent state; a fresh database is reproducible from migrations.

topics.title: Identity & permissions
topics.label: Core delivery
topics.summary: Decide who can see or change each resource.
topics.bridge: Use a small role model before enterprise SSO. Authentication and authorization are separate design decisions.
learn: Distinguish identity verification from resource authorization.
Enforce roles and tenant boundaries on the server.
Understand OAuth/OIDC concepts and use established identity tooling.
topics.artifact: A viewer/operator permission matrix and API tests for denied access.
topics.gate: Changing a resource ID cannot expose another tenant's data; expired or absent credentials are rejected.

topics.title: JavaScript → TypeScript
topics.label: Priority gap
topics.summary: Read and write the browser side of a customer solution.
topics.bridge: Transfer your Python problem-solving habits. Spend time on JavaScript semantics before adding TypeScript types.
learn: Practice arrays, objects, modules, promises, and async/await.
Type API payloads and narrow nullable/error states.
Explain that compile-time types do not validate untrusted network data.
topics.artifact: A typed API client that represents success, empty, loading, and error states.
topics.gate: You can trace a button click through a network request to a rendered result and diagnose a failed call.

topics.title: One useful customer UI
topics.label: Build to learn
topics.summary: Build a screen that helps a user make a decision.
topics.bridge: Apply your Power BI UX instincts to React components, forms, and application state.
learn: Use basic components, state, forms, and accessible labels.
Design loading, empty, error, and retry states.
Add filters and a detail view with clear data freshness.
topics.artifact: A small creator-operations console with filters and an issue detail screen.
topics.gate: A user can complete the intended task with a keyboard and recover from an API failure.

topics.title: Deliver a vertical slice
topics.label: Project 01 gate
topics.summary: Connect the user's action to data, service behavior, and a visible result.
topics.bridge: Extend PixelFed into a product surface. Keep its social-content scope; do not invent sales or ROAS metrics.
learn: Trace a user action across UI, API, and database.
Check data freshness and permissions at integration boundaries.
Write a short demo script and collect structured feedback.
topics.artifact: Project 01: PixelFed Operations Console, with setup instructions and one complete user journey.
topics.gate: A clean checkout supports a working demo and an access-denied demo; limitations and synthetic data are disclosed.

weekly.focus: Put a contract around the data
tasks: Build and test the first FastAPI endpoints.
Add migrations and one atomic operational update.

weekly.focus: Protect resources and learn the browser
tasks: Test viewer/operator and cross-tenant denial cases.
Practice JavaScript async calls and type the API payload.
Create the React filters, metrics view, and detail screen.
Cover loading, empty, stale-data, and error states.
Connect UI, API, and database and test the full journey.
Record Project 01 and ask for feedback against the brief.

phases.title: Add grounded AI
phases.outcome: A workflow support copilot with cited answers, scoped tools, and a small repeatable evaluation set.

topics.title: LLM application basics
topics.label: Build on n8n
topics.summary: Use a model as a fallible component with an explicit contract.
topics.bridge: You have n8n AI Agent, structured output, and sentiment workflows. Add direct SDK calls and controlled experiments.
learn: Explain context, tokens, sampling, and structured output.
Validate outputs and handle rate limits, timeouts, and refusals.
Compare a deterministic solution with an LLM baseline.
topics.artifact: A small support-ticket classifier with a labeled fixture set and a non-LLM baseline.
topics.gate: Malformed output is rejected; the same test cases compare quality, latency, and estimated token cost.

topics.title: RAG with evidence
topics.label: Build on Qdrant
topics.summary: Retrieve authorized evidence and say when it is insufficient.
topics.bridge: Reuse Qdrant from your stack. Start with a small, sanitized set of workflow runbooks, including Arabic and English examples.
learn: Chunk documents and preserve source IDs, versions, and metadata.
Compare retrieval against a keyword baseline.
Filter by access scope and return citations or an explicit no-answer.
topics.artifact: A runbook assistant over sanitized n8n documentation with citations and tenant filters.
topics.gate: Known answers cite the right source; missing evidence and unauthorized documents never produce a fabricated confident answer.

topics.title: Evaluate before you trust
topics.label: Priority gap
topics.summary: Measure failure modes, not just the best-looking response.
topics.bridge: Bring your analyst mindset to AI quality. Treat the evaluation dataset and scoring rules as versioned assets.
learn: Create at least 30 learning cases: routine, ambiguous, missing-evidence, Arabic/English, and adversarial.
Separate retrieval, task success, citation quality, and permission failures.
Record model/prompt versions and measure latency and cost per successful task.
topics.artifact: A versioned eval report with a baseline, failure taxonomy, and a proposed release threshold.
topics.gate: You can reproduce the score and explain the worst failures. A suggested learning target is 80% rubric pass with zero access leaks; negotiate real pilot thresholds with users.

topics.title: Tools with boundaries
topics.label: Core delivery
topics.summary: Give an assistant only the capabilities the task needs.
topics.bridge: Your automation experience helps with tool schemas and side effects. Start read-only, then simulate an approval-gated action.
learn: Define narrow schemas, resource scopes, and server-side validation.
Distinguish model suggestions from authorized execution.
Bound calls and execution time; use idempotency keys for writes.
topics.artifact: Read-only execution-status tools plus a mock proposed retry requiring human approval.
topics.gate: Prompt injection cannot broaden permissions; a repeated approval cannot execute the same side effect twice.

topics.title: Reliable workflow design
topics.label: Build on n8n
topics.summary: Choose a workflow or an agent based on uncertainty and risk.
topics.bridge: Use your n8n queue-mode project as a lab, without assuming its production readiness from the repository description.
learn: Model deterministic paths, retries, dead-letter handling, and human review.
Carry correlation IDs across API, n8n, and database.
Handle duplicate webhooks and partially completed jobs.
topics.artifact: A support-triage workflow with explicit states and a replay-safe failure path.
topics.gate: A duplicate webhook and a crashed dependency do not cause duplicate side effects; failed jobs are visible and recoverable.

topics.title: One narrow MCP server
topics.label: Connect systems
topics.summary: Understand a standard tool boundary by implementing a tiny one.
topics.bridge: Expose an existing read-only capability rather than adding another framework or agent swarm.
learn: Explain host, client, server, tools, and resources.
Validate arguments and scope credentials per tool.
Version the tool contract and report structured errors.
topics.artifact: One read-only workflow-status tool, plus a diagram of its trust boundary.
topics.gate: A client can discover and call the tool; invalid arguments and out-of-scope resources are rejected by the server.

tasks: Compare deterministic and model-based classification.
Record output validation, latency, and token estimates.
Ingest sanitized runbooks with version and access metadata.
Test citations, missing evidence, and Arabic/English queries.
Build the 30-case learning eval set and inspect failures.
Add narrow tools and a mock approval-gated action.
Handle retries, duplicate events, and explicit states in n8n.
Expose one read-only MCP tool and document the trust boundary.

phases.title: Make it dependable
phases.outcome: Project 02: a deployable Support Copilot with telemetry, a recovery drill, and release checks.

topics.title: Reproducible containers
topics.label: Build on Docker
topics.summary: Make local success reproducible on a clean machine.
topics.bridge: Your Docker, Redis, PostgreSQL, and n8n troubleshooting gives you useful context. Practice with a small isolated lab stack.
learn: Pin compatible versions, configure health checks, and separate config from secrets.
Understand networks, named volumes, and resource limits.
Verify backup and restore rather than only creating backup files.
topics.artifact: A minimal Compose stack for API, database, and copilot dependencies, with a restore drill.
topics.gate: A clean startup works; a recreated container preserves intended data; a backup restores into a separate test instance.

topics.title: One cloud, end to end
topics.label: Priority gap
topics.summary: Deploy one service and understand the infrastructure it depends on.
topics.bridge: Azure is a reasonable learning default beside your Microsoft BI tools. Choose one cloud; do not learn three at once.
learn: Map identity, compute, networking, storage, and managed database.
Configure TLS, environment separation, and a budget alert.
Compare a managed service with self-hosting using explicit tradeoffs.
topics.artifact: A deployment diagram and a small pilot environment, or a reproducible local simulation if a paid account is unavailable.
topics.gate: You can explain the request path, service identity, secret source, and shutdown procedure. Record any untested cloud assumptions.

topics.title: Security & data boundaries
topics.label: Non-negotiable
topics.summary: Treat data movement and tool permissions as design decisions.
topics.bridge: Extend your local-network and access-control work into application and AI threat modeling.
learn: Map sensitive data, entry points, credentials, and tenant boundaries.
Apply least privilege, output validation, log redaction, and retention limits.
Test prompt injection and unauthorized access; document residual risks.
topics.artifact: A small threat model and abuse-case test report for Project 02.
topics.gate: No secret enters a client bundle or committed fixture; denied requests remain denied across API, retrieval, and tools.

topics.title: Logs, metrics & traces
topics.label: See the system
topics.summary: Explain what happened to one user request across the stack.
topics.bridge: Use your dashboard skills on operational measurements: task success, failures, queue delay, latency, and freshness.
learn: Carry a correlation ID and redact sensitive log fields.
Define service and task-level indicators with an agreed observation window.
Follow one failed request through a distributed trace or correlated logs.
topics.artifact: An operations view with p50/p95 latency, error rate, queue delay, and cost per successful task.
topics.gate: A simulated failure can be traced to its cause; the dashboard distinguishes a healthy process from a successful user task.

topics.title: Failure & recovery drills
topics.label: Prove reliability
topics.summary: Practice the failures a demo usually hides.
topics.bridge: Turn your Redis and n8n debugging experience into a repeatable diagnostic method and a tested recovery procedure.
learn: Use bounded retries, backoff, idempotency, and dead-letter states.
Inject a dependency outage, duplicate event, and malformed payload.
Measure recovery time and data loss against explicit learning objectives.
topics.artifact: A failure matrix and recovery drill report with commands, expected state, and evidence.
topics.gate: Restore and replay are tested in the lab; observed recovery time and data loss are reported honestly, with no invented availability claim.

topics.title: CI/CD & safe releases
topics.label: Project 02 gate
topics.summary: Release a known version and know how to recover.
topics.bridge: Build on your GitHub Actions and protected-branch experience. Include API contracts and AI regressions in release decisions.
learn: Run tests and a small eval suite before publishing an artifact.
Separate staging from production and record deployed versions.
Distinguish code rollback from restoring incompatible data migrations.
topics.artifact: Project 02 release checklist, CI pipeline, deployment notes, and rollback/restore procedure.
topics.gate: A failed contract or access test blocks release; a known version can be redeployed and a data-restore limitation is documented.

tasks: Containerize the minimal services with explicit versions.
Restore a backup into a separate lab instance.
Map one-cloud architecture and environment configuration.
Test access, prompt injection, secret handling, and log redaction.
Instrument task success, latency, queue delay, and cost.
Run dependency-outage, duplicate-event, and recovery drills.
Gate the release on tests and the versioned eval set.
Record a demo, known limitations, and rollback/restore instructions.

phases.title: Lead the customer pilot
phases.outcome: A capstone pilot plan with agreed acceptance criteria, feedback evidence, and an operational handover.

topics.title: Scope & stakeholder alignment
topics.label: Customer craft
topics.summary: Turn a promising prototype into a bounded delivery commitment.
topics.bridge: Use your BI requirements experience, then add a stakeholder map and an explicit acceptance decision.
learn: Run a discovery simulation with user, sponsor, and technical-owner perspectives.
Separate must-haves from requests and maintain an assumptions log.
Agree deliverables, exclusions, dependencies, and escalation paths.
topics.artifact: A pilot brief and stakeholder map for a fictional Egyptian cosmetics distributor.
topics.gate: A reviewer can identify the pilot owner, a single target workflow, and what is excluded from this iteration.

topics.title: Explain architecture tradeoffs
topics.label: Decision-making
topics.summary: Make an engineering choice understandable to both users and engineers.
topics.bridge: Extend your lakehouse and galaxy diagrams into request flows, trust boundaries, and decision records.
learn: Draw a system context and one end-to-end sequence.
Compare build/buy, workflow/agent, and managed/self-hosted options.
Write a decision record with consequences and a revisit trigger.
topics.artifact: Two architecture diagrams and a one-page decision record for the capstone.
topics.gate: You can explain a rejected option and the condition under which it would become preferable.

topics.title: Demos & feedback loops
topics.label: Customer craft
topics.summary: Use a demo to learn whether the workflow is useful.
topics.bridge: Your dashboard storytelling translates well. Add a task-based usability session with structured notes.
learn: Demo the user's before-and-after workflow in five minutes.
Ask a reviewer to complete a task without coaching.
Turn observed friction into a prioritized issue with a clear acceptance test.
topics.artifact: A demo script, feedback log, and three prioritized changes.
topics.gate: Separate actual reviewer feedback from your own hypotheses; if no reviewer is available, label the exercise as a self-review.

topics.title: Measure value & adoption
topics.label: Build on analytics
topics.summary: Show what improved, for whom, and at what cost.
topics.bridge: This is where your KPI and Power BI background is an advantage. Add adoption and total operating cost to the story.
learn: Compare task completion and handling time with a stated baseline.
Measure adoption, rework, failure rate, and cost per successful task.
Separate measured pilot results from estimated business value.
topics.artifact: A pilot scorecard with a small sensitivity analysis and assumptions.
topics.gate: Benefits are reproducible from evidence; projected EGP savings are labeled estimates and include labor and API/cloud assumptions.

topics.title: Enablement & handover
topics.label: Ownership transfer
topics.summary: Leave behind a system someone else can operate.
topics.bridge: Turn your technical walkthroughs into a short operator guide and a clear ownership agreement.
learn: Write a user quickstart, operator runbook, and troubleshooting decision tree.
Document credentials ownership, escalation, backup, and change procedures.
Train a reviewer through one routine task and one failure case.
topics.artifact: A handover pack and a teach-back checklist.
topics.gate: A reviewer can follow the runbook without undocumented help; any simulated training is labeled as such.

topics.title: Incident communication
topics.label: Own the outcome
topics.summary: Communicate clearly when a customer's workflow breaks.
topics.bridge: Build on your evidence-first troubleshooting: state impact, current facts, next action, and the next update time.
learn: Triage an incident with impact, severity, and containment.
Write a plain-language status update and a technical timeline.
Produce a blameless root-cause analysis with corrective actions.
topics.artifact: A simulated incident update and postmortem for a queue or retrieval failure.
topics.gate: The update distinguishes known facts from hypotheses; every corrective action has an owner and a verification step.

tasks: Draft the Egyptian SME pilot brief and stakeholder map.
Agree acceptance criteria and exclusions in a discovery simulation.
Draw architecture and write one decision record.
Create a before/after demo and collect task-based feedback.
Build a baseline/value/adoption scorecard.
Write a user guide and operator handover runbook.
Run a handover teach-back or labeled self-review.
Simulate an incident and write an update and postmortem.

phases.title: Prove the whole journey
phases.outcome: Project 03: a portfolio pilot demonstrating discovery, implementation, measurement, and handover.

topics.title: Freeze the capstone slice
topics.label: Project 03
topics.summary: Choose a small workflow and make its acceptance tests explicit.
topics.bridge: Use an Egyptian SME operations scenario to connect SQL, BI, API development, and n8n without starting a sprawling new platform.
learn: Choose stock exceptions or order reconciliation for a fictional distributor.
Use labeled synthetic order/inventory fixtures with documented EGP assumptions.
Define success, access, correctness, performance, and recovery checks.
topics.artifact: A final implementation plan, data contract, test fixtures, and acceptance checklist.
topics.gate: One user, one workflow, one measurable outcome, and a documented data provenance story fit in a two-minute explanation.

topics.title: Build the pilot system
topics.label: Integrate your stack
topics.summary: Connect the smallest system that completes the workflow.
topics.bridge: Reuse components and lessons from Projects 01 and 02. AI is optional unless it improves the chosen task.
learn: Connect React, FastAPI, PostgreSQL, and an n8n integration.
Preserve permission boundaries and audit operational actions.
Keep any assistant read-only or approval-gated and show its evidence.
topics.artifact: A working exception-to-resolution flow with a reproducible fixture and audit trail.
topics.gate: The user completes the workflow from the UI; the backend validates actions, records outcomes, and handles a retry safely.

topics.title: Validate with a user lens
topics.label: Acceptance gate
topics.summary: Check usability, correctness, and failure behavior against the agreed scope.
topics.bridge: Use the same measurement discipline you apply to a BI model. Make failed checks visible rather than hiding them in the demo.
learn: Run happy-path, access, empty-data, duplicate-event, and dependency-failure scenarios.
Use a reviewer or explicitly labeled self-review.
If AI is present, run the fixed eval set and record remaining failures.
topics.artifact: An acceptance report with evidence, open issues, and the release recommendation.
topics.gate: Every agreed criterion is passed or explicitly deferred with impact; no access-control failure is waved through.

topics.title: Plan rollout & ownership
topics.label: Operational gate
topics.summary: Show how a pilot becomes a maintained workflow.
topics.bridge: Combine your Docker runbooks, CI habits, and handover practice into one deployment story.
learn: Define a staged rollout, monitoring checks, and a stop condition.
Run a backup/restore or rollback drill in the lab.
Assign operational ownership and document ongoing cost assumptions.
topics.artifact: A pilot release pack with deployment, recovery, monitoring, and handover instructions.
topics.gate: A reviewer can start the lab, run the workflow, identify a failure, and recover using the documented procedure.

topics.title: Publish the case study
topics.label: Portfolio evidence
topics.summary: Tell the engineering story with evidence and honest limits.
topics.bridge: Link your existing portfolio, PixelFed, and n8n repos to a complete customer-outcome narrative.
learn: Explain problem, discovery, architecture, tradeoffs, delivery, and results.
Include screenshots, diagrams, a five-minute demo, and reproduction steps.
Label fictional customers, synthetic data, simulations, and unmeasured projections.
topics.artifact: A case study, architecture diagrams, demo video, and public sanitized repository.
topics.gate: A hiring reviewer can see your own contribution, run the demo, and distinguish measured outcomes from learning targets.

topics.title: FDE interview & role fit
topics.label: Next chapter
topics.summary: Practice ambiguous problems, code, and customer conversations.
topics.bridge: Position yourself around data and AI integration delivery. Remote Solutions Engineer, Implementation Engineer, and AI Integration Engineer roles may also fit your constraint set.
learn: Practice Python/SQL coding, practical data structures, and API debugging.
Run a 45-minute discovery-to-design case and explain tradeoffs aloud.
Screen each job for country eligibility, remote policy, travel, seniority, and customer duties.
topics.artifact: Three mock cases, a concise project narrative, and a role-fit checklist.
topics.gate: You can scope an ambiguous customer problem, implement a small integration, explain failure recovery, and discuss a real tradeoff. This plan builds evidence; it does not guarantee role readiness or a job.

tasks: Freeze the scope, fixtures, and acceptance checklist.
Reuse existing components to connect the first full workflow.
Complete UI, API, database, and workflow integration.
Run user-task, permission, and failure acceptance scenarios.
Run deployment/recovery and monitoring checks.
Publish the case study, diagrams, and a five-minute demo.
Run three discovery, coding/debugging, and system-design mock cases.
Use the role-fit checklist to target eligible remote opportunities.

projects.title: PixelFed Operations Console
projects.subtitle: Turn analytics into an application
projects.problem: A fictional community operations team needs to investigate creator activity and stale metrics without moving between raw tables and reports.
projects.reuse: Extend your existing PixelFed data contracts and gold-level analytics. All records remain synthetic; this is a learning build, not a real customer engagement.
deliverables: A discovery brief and metric/freshness contract
A read-only metrics API plus a small operational issue table
An accessible console with filters, detail views, and explicit error states
A tested permissions matrix and a short user-task demo
projects.success: A reviewer can investigate one activity anomaly from the UI, trace its source, and explain data freshness. Unauthorized access tests pass.

projects.title: Workflow Support Copilot
projects.subtitle: Add intelligence you can inspect
projects.problem: A fictional automation operator needs to find the right runbook, inspect a failed execution, and decide what action is safe.
projects.reuse: Use sanitized runbooks and a lab copy of your n8n stack. Credentials and production execution data do not enter the public demo.
deliverables: A cited English/Arabic runbook assistant with permission-aware retrieval
A versioned 30-case learning eval set and a keyword baseline
Read-only execution tools plus a mock human-approved retry
A deployment, telemetry, and recovery drill report
projects.success: Suggested learning target: at least 80% rubric pass on the fixed learning set, zero access leaks, and no duplicate simulated action. Report actual latency/cost; real pilot targets require agreement.

principles.title: Use what you already know
principles.text: Keep Python, SQL, Power BI, n8n, and PostgreSQL. Add FastAPI and enough React/TypeScript for a useful interface. Choose one cloud.

principles.title: Earn progress with evidence
principles.text: Every topic starts at zero. Existing exposure is marked as a starting advantage; mark a topic complete when you can meet its exit check.

principles.title: Make room for customer work
principles.text: Practice discovery, demos, tradeoffs, documentation, and handover every week. A working model is only one component of delivery.

principles.title: Build for your constraints
principles.text: Plan for 9 hours a week: roughly 2 learning, 5 building, 1 validation, and 1 communication. Use small fixtures and one lab stack; stretch the timeline when needed.
